- Session: `session_01B3Kurx8qufrDzNjk4rag7V` (account `hotlong`)
- Branch: `claude/issue-7653-ai-anon-deny-ordering`
- Worktree: dedicated (cloud container)
- Domain: `domain:cli`
- File surface: `packages/runtime/src/domains/ai.ts` (the `handleAIRequest` entry region ~:68-79 and the gate site ~:128) + its tests. Stop on breach; explain in the report.
- Container & model: M, `mode:cloud` (dedicated container, per #7341), `model: claude-opus-5`.
- Serial constraints cleared: `runtime/src/domains/ai.ts` is touched by none of the four in-flight cli claims — #6599 (`rest-server.ts` `_drafts` region + `runtime/domains/meta.ts`), #7645 (`packages/mcp`), #7661 (`runtime/src/sandbox/**`), #7578 (`runtime/domains/packages.ts`). Disjoint.

### Scope boundary (the card is explicit and I am holding it)

⛔ **The honest-degradation half PASSES and must not be "fixed"** — `/ai/models`, `/conversations`, `/usage`, `/chat` answering 501 with the Cloud/EE remedy sentence (never 404/503), `/ai/agents` returning the declared envelope, and `/discovery`'s `services.ai` message being string-identical to the 501 body are all correct today. A diff that changes any of them is a regression.

The defect in scope is **ordering only**: `handleAIRequest` returns the `/ai/agents` courtesy and `capabilityUnavailable(deps, 'ai')` at the top of the handler, while `shouldDenyAnonymous` sits inside the per-route loop below — reachable only when the AI service is serveable. So on every open-edition deployment the whole `/ai/**` family answers unauthenticated callers before the anonymous gate is consulted.

### Pin the consequence, in the order the contract states

The three-way assertion the card measured is the acceptance criterion: unauth `/ai/models` → **401** (not 501), unauth `/ai/agents` → **401** (not 200), and the control — anonymous `/api/v1/data/showcase_task` → **401** — still correct, proving the gate was live on the same boot and this is ordering rather than absence. Add the authenticated-caller cases too: with a valid principal the 501s and the `/ai/agents` envelope must come back **unchanged**, or "fixed the ordering" has silently become "broke the degradation".

⚠️ Reverse-verify: with the reordering reverted, the two 401 assertions must go red and the degradation assertions must stay green.

## ACCEPTED — PR #7910. Landing held on the gate jobs.

Reviewed by the `domain:cli` seat (`hotlong`, session `session_01B3Kurx8qufrDzNjk4rag7V`) against the diff.

**The ordering fix is the shape I asked for, and the part I most wanted is there.** The anonymous decision is computed **once** at the top of `handleAIRequest` and consulted at each exit — not duplicated into two call sites. A rule with two copies is the drift class this repo keeps paying for (#7616 exists because of it), so "hoist the gate" had a wrong way to do it and this is not that.

**Group C is the control that decides whether this is a fix or a blunt instrument.** A route declaring `auth: false` still **serves** anonymous callers. A change that simply 401s everyone would satisfy every positive case in Group A and still be a regression — that case is what tells the two apart, and the reasoning behind keeping the per-route opt-out down in the loop (only a *registered* route can declare it; with no serveable service there is no route to declare it, so the family default stands) is correct rather than convenient.

**The honest-degradation half is pinned as hard as the defect**, which was the explicit boundary: 501 for `/ai/models` `/conversations` `/usage` `/chat` — never 404, never 503 — carrying `serviceUnavailableMessage('ai')`; `/ai/agents` returning the payload **relocated** under `data.agents` rather than flattened (a flatten makes `useAiSurfaceEnabled` hide the entire AI surface, #4053); and the 501 body asserted **string-identical** to `/discovery`'s `services.ai` message against the single producer, not by substring. Internal `isSystem` callers still reach the degradation answers.

**Group D is beyond the brief and correct**: the unpublished-route-table exit (`AI routes not yet initialized`, 503) is also gated, because a boot-race window answering "AI is mounted, come back shortly" is the same disclosure by another door.

**On the modified existing tests — the thing I check hardest.** Three pre-existing cases were given authenticated contexts. That is the pattern that launders a regression, so: they ran through `dispatch()`, which re-resolves identity off the auth-less mock kernel, meaning they were measuring the courtesy **as an anonymous caller — through the very hole being closed**. Re-pointing them at an authenticated principal is what makes them mean what their names claim, and the dev did not simply delete the anonymous coverage: a new registry-path case asserts `/ai/agents` and `/ai/chat` return `401 UNAUTHENTICATED` through the full `dispatch()` path. Coverage moved, and grew.

`error` is wired to the **real** `apiErrorResponse` rather than a stub that drops the third argument — without that, `details.code` would never be promoted and every `code` assertion would be vacuous. That is the ADR-0112-envelope-test-that-asserts-nothing trap, avoided deliberately.

**Scope**: `packages/runtime/**` + changeset. Beyond the `domains/ai.ts` I declared, it touches two runtime **test** files for the reason above — test-only, disclosed, justified. No `docs/adr/**`, no skills paths, no `content/docs/releases/`.

⛔ Not flipped yet: ESLint and TypeScript Type Check must both read `conclusion: success` first. ⚠️ Same risk flagged on #7908 — sibling PR #7907 tripped the `check:type-check-debt` ratchet on new `packages/runtime` test-layer type errors, and this PR adds a 286-line runtime test file. If it trips, the new tests get typed correctly; ⛔ the ledger will not be raised.
